prerequisites: Express ideas with order, clarity, conciseness, and correctness using appropriate mathematical symbolic language.
Have sufficient command of elementary arithmetic, basic geometry, and fluid mental calculations.
Know how to interpret and geometrically represent abstract results.

Master certain calculations: operations with matrices and determinants, solving systems of linear equations, obtaining primitive functions of elementary functions, solving definite and indefinite integrals of simple functions.
Ability to read, understand, and assimilate mathematical texts.
Aptitude and attitude for group work.
Develop good study techniques based on adequate note-taking, bibliographic search, and reading comprehension.
Motivation, responsibility, involvement, and demandingness for daily work required by continuous assessment.

learning_outcomes.text: Ability to solve mathematical problems that may arise in engineering. Aptitude to apply knowledge of: linear algebra; geometry; differential geometry; differential and integral calculus; differential and partial differential equations; numerical methods; numerical algorithmics; statistics and optimization.
Basic knowledge about the use and programming of computers, operating systems, databases, and computer programs with application in engineering.
Adopt a responsible, orderly attitude at work and be willing to learn, considering the challenge that continuous training will pose.
Apply the strategies of the scientific methodology: analyze the situation and problems qualitatively and quantitatively. Pose hypotheses and solutions using models typical of industrial engineering.
Work effectively in a group, integrating capacities and knowledge to make decisions in the field of industrial engineering.
Relationally identify the concepts of Linear Algebra and Geometry to analyze Engineering problems efficiently using both an algebraic and a numerical approach.
Critically develop valid conclusions (reasoned and justified) from the produced results, based on optimal management of information acquired from problematic situations in Engineering.
Effectively communicate orally and in writing the methodologies and skills acquired using appropriate language, terminology, and resources.

syllabus_topics: Matrix operations: matrix addition, product of a matrix and a scalar, product of two matrices, power of square matrices (induction method)
Inverse matrix: adjoint method, Gauss method
Special types of matrices: symmetric matrix, antisymmetric matrix, periodic matrix, idempotent matrix, involutive matrix, nilpotent matrix, and orthogonal matrix
Linear equation and homogeneous linear equation
System of linear equations: non-homogeneous and homogeneous system of linear equations
Representation of a system of linear equations: general representation, vectorial representation, and matrix representation
Solution of a system of linear equations
Classification of a system of linear equations: determined compatible system, undetermined compatible system, incompatible system
Solving a system of linear equations: Gauss method, Gauss-Jordan method
Examples of vector spaces: real vector space of dimension n, matrix space of dimension mxn, polynomial space of degree less than or equal to n
Vector subspace generated by a finite system of vectors, linear closure
Linear dependence and independence: free system of vectors and bound system of vectors
Basis and dimension of a vector subspace
Coordinates of a vector in a basis
Operations with vector subspaces: intersection, sum, and direct sum
Examples of Euclidean vector spaces: real vector space of dimension n, matrix space of dimension mxn, polynomial space of degree less than or equal to n
Norm associated with a scalar product
Matrix expression of the scalar product (Gram matrix)
Orthogonality and orthonormality: orthogonal vectors, unit vectors
System of orthogonal vectors and system of orthonormal vectors
Orthogonal complement of a vector subspace
Linear approximation: orthogonal projection onto a subspace, Fourier coefficients
Approximate solution by least squares of an incompatible system of linear equations
Concept of eigenvalues and eigenvectors: spectrum of a matrix
Characteristic polynomial and characteristic equation: calculation of eigenvalues and eigenvectors
Multiplicity algebraic and geometric of an eigenvalue
Diagonalization by similarity of a square matrix
Diagonalization of real symmetric matrices by orthogonal similarity

assessment_methods.method: Written test (Final Exercise) for continuous evaluation
Practical applications with computer tool for continuous evaluation
Computer tool knowledge test for final evaluation

assessment_rules: Continuous evaluation is preferred and consists of a final written exercise (55%), practical exercises (25%), and computer tool applications (20%). To pass continuous evaluation, a minimum of 40% (4 out of 10) is required in the final written exercise, and the overall weighted sum must be 50% or higher, otherwise the final grade is 4.5. Students can opt for final evaluation, which includes a theoretical-practical test (80%) and a computer tool knowledge test (20%), with a minimum of 40% required in the theoretical-practical test, otherwise the final grade is 4.5. For the extraordinary call, continuous assessment grades can be carried over if they exceed 50% by written request; otherwise, the final evaluation system applies with its requirements.
